elements.requirement: Section 238 applies in the case of a company where the company enters administration or the company goes into liquidation.
elements.quote: This section applies in the case of a company where— (a) the company enters administration, (b) the company goes into liquidation

elements.requirement: For a company that enters administration or goes into liquidation, the office-holder means the administrator or the liquidator, as the case may be.
elements.quote: “the office-holder” means the administrator or the liquidator, as the case may be

elements.requirement: The administrator or liquidator of a company may apply to the court for an order where the company has entered into a transaction with any person at an undervalue at a relevant time defined in section 240.
elements.quote: the office-holder may apply to the court for an order under this section

elements.requirement: Subject to subsection (5), the court must, on an application by the office-holder, make such order as the court thinks fit for restoring the position to what it would have been if the company had not entered into the transaction at an undervalue.
elements.quote: the court shall, on such an application, make such order as it thinks fit for restoring the position to what it would have been if the company had not entered into that transaction

elements.requirement: A company enters into a transaction with a person at an undervalue for the purposes of section 238 and section 241 if the company makes a gift to that person or otherwise enters into a transaction with that person on terms that provide for the company to receive no consideration.
elements.quote: the company makes a gift to that person or otherwise enters into a transaction with that person on terms that provide for the company to receive no consideration

elements.requirement: A company enters into a transaction with a person at an undervalue for the purposes of section 238 and section 241 if the company enters into a transaction with that person for a consideration the value of which, in money or money’s worth, is significantly less than the value, in money or money’s worth, of the consideration provided by the company.
elements.quote: the company enters into a transaction with that person for a consideration the value of which, in money or money’s worth, is significantly less than the value, in money or money’s worth, of the consideration provided by the company

elements.requirement: The court must not make an order in respect of a transaction at an undervalue if the court is satisfied that the company entered into the transaction in good faith and for the purpose of carrying on its business, and that at the time the company did so there were reasonable grounds for believing that the transaction would benefit the company.
elements.quote: The court shall not make an order under this section in respect of a transaction at an undervalue if it is satisfied— (a) that the company which entered into the transaction did so in good faith and for the purpose of carrying on its business, and (b) that at the time it did so there were reasonable grounds for believing that the transaction would benefit the company
